candidates.title: Loud backlash vs measured response: John Lewis 'Gloria and Pickles' Christmas ad
candidates.publisher: The Drum (column by Andrew Tindall, System1)
candidates.claim: System1 Test Your Ad (nationally representative UK sample, 'hundreds of people', size not given): 69% responded positively, 10% negatively, 6% felt contempt; 5.6 Stars, best John Lewis Christmas ad since 2019. 'Online, that 10% can feel like 30% or even 50%.'
candidates.verification: Cross-checked: DesignRush (2026-11-04) reports the same 5.6 Stars plus OnePulse (68% liked/loved; 36% more likely to shop, 58% no difference) and Kantar expert view ('lacks the emotive punch'); Brit Brief (2026-11-04) and DesignRush document the press/social backlash (Sarah Vine, The Independent 'tone deaf', Piers Morgan). Caveats: System1 is the columnist's employer; sample size not published; no sales data yet. Supporting evergreen: Pew 2019, ~10% of US Twitter users write ~80% of tweets (Poynter).
candidates.note: Strongest tension of the night: the comment section is not the market. Highly usable for small owners who change course after a few angry reviews.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C1: two independent outlets on 2026-11-04 report the System1 5.6 Stars; the 69%/10%/6% split comes from the System1 executive's own column (vendor interest, sample size unpublished). OnePulse 68% liked/loved is a second, independent-ish measure pointing the same way. Kantar's expert view is more critical: do not claim 'everyone loved it'. No sales data yet: never claim the ad 'worked' commercially. The Pew 10%/80% figure is from 2019 and about Twitter in the US: use only as a general illustration, in the caption, with year. Do not quote Piers Morgan or name columnists on screen.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Every business owner has felt the sting of one loud review. The reel gives relief plus a tool: noise is not a vote. Negativity is more shareable (The Drum cites Cambridge research, 1.91x; secondary, caption only if used). Risk: sounding like 'ignore critics'. Frame: listen to criticism, but weigh it; measure the silent majority (repeat customers, orders, a quick question to ten regulars).
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Squarely brand strategy and communication: how to read reaction to a campaign, rebrand or new pack. Works for a café owner and for a CMO, and for Persian and international audiences alike. Not a repeat: last 7 days were memory, logos, pricing, naming, borrowed fame.

gates.brand_fit_gate: C1 passes. C2, C4 fail repeat gate; C5, C6 near-repeat; C8, C9, C10 fail verification (headline only).
gates.story_gate: C1: tension = 'the loudest voices feel like everyone, but they are a few'; concrete image = a megaphone shouting at a room where most people are quietly nodding. Beats C3 (good line, stale news, split idea) and C11 (warm, weak tension).

decision.why: Highest score (90, estimate), strongest tension and image, high utility for small owners, verified by multiple same-day sources with honest caveats.
